This is revenue.
And this is
profit.
But what's the
difference?
Revenue is the
total money a
business earns from
selling products or
services.
Profit is what's
left after subtracting
expenses.
For example,
if a business
earns $10,000 and
spends $7,000,
its profit is
$3,000.
Now,
what about assets
and liabilities?
Assets are valuable
things a business
owns,
like cash,
buildings,
and equipment.
Liabilities are what
a business owes,
like loans,
unpaid bills,
and debts.
Revenue is earned.
Profit is what's
left.
Assets are owned.
Liabilities are owed.
